money-laundering.title: Money laundering
money-laundering.extract:
Money laundering is the process of illegally concealing the origin of money obtained from illicit activities (often known as dirty money), and converting the funds into a seemingly legitimate source. As financial crime has become more complex and financial intelligence is more important in combating international crime and terrorism, money laundering has become the subject of prominent political, economic, and legal debate. Most countries implement some anti-money-laundering measures.

housing-bubble.title: Housing bubble
housing-bubble.extract: A housing bubble (or housing price bubble) is one of several types of asset price bubbles which periodically occur in the market. The basic concept of a housing bubble is the same as for other asset bubbles, consisting of two main phases. First there is a period where house prices increase dramatically, driven by real estate investing. In the second phase, house prices fall dramatically, making housing more affordable. neoliberalism.title: Neoliberalism
neoliberalism.extract: Neoliberalism is a political and economic ideology that advocates for free-market capitalism and developed from challenges to  classical liberalism in the early 20th century. It advocates policies that became dominant from the late 20th century that promote market processes and competition. The term has multiple, competing definitions, and is often used pejoratively.
